bloques.titulo: The case agreement in the position
texto: A position works as an explanatory parenthesis that shares the syntactic function of the nucleus to which it is accompanied:
1. **En nominativo**: * * Frau Dr. Weber, - die renommierte Expertin, - übernimmt die Führung * * (subject).
2. **En dativo**: **Wir gratulieren Herrn Becker, [unserem erfahrenen Ingenieur], zum Erfolg** (object in dative).
3. **En acusativo**: **Sie wählten Herrn Klein, [einen geschätzten Kollegen], zum Sprecher** (object in accusative).
4. **En genitivo**: **Das Votum des Aufsichtsrats, [unseres obersten Kontrollgremiums], war eindeutig** (name plugin).
It is a frequent error not to close the position with the second coma when the main prayer continues.

bloques.pregunta: What grammatical case should the explanatory position be adopted in German?

opciones.texto: The same grammatical case as the noun he complements and explains.
opciones.explicacion: The position is strictly in line with its reference term.

opciones.texto: Always the nominating case, no matter the rest of the sentence.

opciones.texto: They must be defined by two commas: one of opening and one of closing.
opciones.explicacion: «Frau Weber, die neue Leiterin, spricht heute zu uns».

opciones.texto: Only coma is placed at the beginning of the position, never at the end.
opciones.explicacion: Allowing the closing coma is a serious orthographic lack in German.

opciones.texto: No coma is put on if the position has more than three words.
opciones.explicacion: The comma delimitation is applied regardless of length.

bloques.frase: Das Urteil des Richters, ___ erfahrenen Juristen, stieß auf breite Zustimmung.

opciones.explicacion: As the «des Richters» core is in genitive, the position requires the genitive «eines».
